results.description:
. Chinese Jet-Fuel Refinery to Bypass Sanctions, Myanmar’s Blood Timber Flows to China, and More 
Myanmar’s military regime has restarted the Thanlyin No.1 Oil Refinery near Yangon, allowing it to bypass jet fuel sanctions and sustain its deadly air raids on the civilian population. 
According to Nikkei Asia, Phase 1 is designed to produce 150,000 metric tons of jet fuel annually, roughly equal to Myanmar’s import volume last year.

results.title: Like with Russia, Trump will fail with Myanmar.
results.description:
Like with Russia, Trump will fail with Myanmar. China is already there and will be the main trading partner in the next decade. What ever Trump wants to extract from Myanmar, will need Chinas approval. 
Relations between Myanmar and China are close and shaped by strategic, economic, and geopolitical self-interest.  China is Myanmar’s most important trading partner, primary source of imports, and largest investor. Bilateral trade volume stood at approximately $19.4 billion in 2025 (a 19.1% increase from the previous year).  As part of China’s “New Silk Road” (Belt and Road Initiative), Beijing is expanding the economic corridor to gain direct land and infrastructure access to the Indian Ocean via Myanmar. China exports vehicles and electromechanical equipment to Myanmar and, in return, imports mineral resources (such as rare earths and mining products) as well as agricultural goods
